taxonomy.name: Compute and model serving
taxonomy.description: From chips and cloud capacity to training, post-training and production inference.

children.name: Chips and physical infrastructure
children.thesis: As training and inference scale, the bottleneck moves to HBM, interconnect, racks and power. Specialized chips compete on model fit and cost per task.
children.bottleneck: Memory bandwidth, interconnect, power delivery and full-system delivery
children.watch: Compare chips by the models they can deploy, total cost of ownership and software migration cost.

children.name: GPU clouds and compute scheduling
children.thesis: Neoclouds are extending from renting GPUs for training into inference and rollouts. Long-term capacity supply is still the main story; utilization, scheduling and service capability decide the incremental value.
children.bottleneck: GPU availability, cluster utilization and capital turnover
children.watch: Look at funding, backlog, revenue and gross margin separately. Reselling long-term compute contracts is not software revenue.

children.name: Training and post-training platforms
children.thesis: Application companies, not only model labs, are starting to buy post-training capability. Demand is extending from fine-tuning tools to RL, distributed rollouts and reproducible experiments.
children.bottleneck: Training stability, feedback quality and iteration cost
children.watch: Separate platform fees from GPU consumption. Whether a customer keeps iterating matters more than the size of one training run.

children.name: Inference engines and services
children.thesis: Once inference volume takes off, scheduling, batching, caching, quantization and model-specific optimization are worth more. The unit of delivery moves from GPU hours to usable throughput and cost per task.
children.bottleneck: Balancing latency, GPU memory, throughput and cost per task
children.watch: Read revenue growth together with GPU cost and gross margin. Model API price cuts raise usage and compress unit price at the same time.

taxonomy.name: Data and knowledge infrastructure
taxonomy.description: Data persistence, real-time state, machine retrieval and long-term context.

children.name: Databases and real-time state
children.thesis: Expanding from document retrieval to agent state, real-time context and reproducible data. Platforms are acquiring their way to a unified data layer that holds this state.
children.bottleneck: State consistency, data freshness and multimodal I/O
children.watch: A general-purpose database platform's revenue cannot all be attributed to agents.

children.name: Search, retrieval and knowledge processing
children.thesis: Machine search is becoming repeat consumption inside reasoning and verification. Owning the index and the data acquisition gives more pricing power than wrapping a search API.
children.bottleneck: Coverage, freshness and citable retrieval results
children.watch: Distinguish proprietary indexes, content extraction, embeddings and resold traffic.

children.name: Memory and context
children.thesis: Value comes from task state and behavioral data that can be updated and moved. The ceiling for a general memory API depends on avoiding absorption by the models' native memory.
children.bottleneck: Memory updates, cross-session consistency and portability
children.watch: Combined-round funding and vague revenue figures cannot be forced into a single quarter.

taxonomy.name: Training data and feedback
taxonomy.description: From expert and synthetic data to trajectories, task environments and verifiers.

children.name: Expert, labeling and synthetic data
children.thesis: Moving from general labeling to expert tasks, agent trajectories and failure cases. Commercial value depends on repeatedly delivering distributions that improve models.
children.bottleneck: Expert supply, task quality and repeatable delivery
children.watch: Gross service revenue may include payments to experts; do not value it as net software ARR.

children.name: Agent trajectories and RL environments
children.thesis: Interactive task environments package data, actions and verifiers together. They extend the post-training data supply chain, and concentrated lab purchasing creates a near-term volume opportunity.
children.bottleneck: Environment realism, task difficulty and verifiers that cannot be gamed
children.watch: A high funding valuation does not mean recurring revenue exists. Watch customer concentration and reuse across scenarios.

children.name: Simulation and physical AI data
children.thesis: What simulation and world-model companies can deliver includes physical interaction data and reproducible scenarios. Some are economically closer to data suppliers.
children.bottleneck: Physical consistency, scenario coverage and sim-to-real transfer
children.watch: Distinguish research models, simulation tools and paid data delivery. A generated video demo is not a usable training environment.

taxonomy.name: Execution and runtime
taxonomy.description: Letting agents execute in isolation, operate real systems and resume tasks.

children.name: Sandboxes and isolated execution
children.thesis: Code execution is turning from an add-on tool into a task primitive. Isolation, snapshots and lifecycle management decide who can carry agent execution at scale.
children.bottleneck: Isolation, start-up speed, snapshots and concurrency
children.watch: Leading in capital raised and leading in production use are different rankings.

children.name: Browser and computer use
children.thesis: Systems without APIs still need browser execution. Production value lies in sessions, identity, failure handling and action verification, not in one successful demo.
children.bottleneck: Stable sessions and task success rate
children.watch: Sandbox deployments, session counts and successfully completed tasks are not interchangeable.

children.name: Durable execution and scheduling
children.thesis: Long tasks make retries, recovery, state and human approval necessary. Value rises with task complexity and does not disappear as model API prices fall.
children.bottleneck: Long-lived state, failure recovery and traceable execution
children.watch: Separate existing revenue from general workflows from new agent usage.

taxonomy.name: Development and integration
taxonomy.description: Connecting tools, writing agents and building enterprise workflows.

children.name: Tool connectivity and integration
children.thesis: Agents need executable actions, delegated credentials and audited writes. The number of connectors becomes a commercial asset only with sustained use and permission management.
children.bottleneck: Connection reliability, delegated authorization and permission boundaries
children.watch: Track one-off integration revenue and ongoing per-call revenue separately.

children.name: Agent development frameworks
children.thesis: Model capability and protocols are absorbing thin orchestration. Independent frameworks need production deployment, observability, distribution or enterprise adoption to earn recurring revenue.
children.bottleneck: Converting open-source developer use into paid production use
children.watch: Downloads, stars, funding and ARR are different metrics. Being consolidated into a platform does not by itself prove the business failed.

children.name: Workflow and app building
children.thesis: Workflows embed agents in existing business operations. Enterprise connection networks, approvals and distribution can retain platform value; low-barrier orchestration is easier to bundle.
children.bottleneck: Executable integrations, enterprise deployment and long-term retention
children.watch: Separate total platform revenue from new agent revenue. For acquisition prices, distinguish company, team and product.

taxonomy.name: Quality, security and control
taxonomy.description: Production traffic, quality evaluation, identity and runtime governance cut across the whole stack.

children.name: Model routing and gateways
children.thesis: The traffic entry point controls routing, billing and security policy at once. Strategic buyers value the access control point, but traffic volume is not necessarily net revenue.
children.bottleneck: Routing, billing, quotas and governance
children.watch: Keep token transaction volume apart from revenue, and signing apart from closing.

children.name: Evals, observability and regression
children.thesis: Production traces, bad cases and verifiers form the quality feedback loop. Acquisitions by data and APM platforms suggest the control point can be worth more than a standalone tool's distribution.
children.bottleneck: Real failure data, evaluation and release gates
children.watch: For acquisition prices, distinguish official consideration, retention pay and media estimates.

children.name: Security, identity and governance
children.thesis: The main caller is expanding from people to agents, so identity, authorization, policy enforcement and audit enter every action. Established security platforms are consolidating these control planes.
children.bottleneck: Who is executing, with what authorization, and who bears the risk
children.watch: The scale of a general identity platform is not agent identity revenue.

taxonomy.name: Interaction and transaction infrastructure
taxonomy.description: Real-time interaction, communications, payments and commerce components closer to the application.

children.name: Real-time voice and communications
children.thesis: Real-time interaction ties voice models, communications, orchestration and reliability together. Growth is usage-driven, so per-call unit economics need watching too.
children.bottleneck: End-to-end latency, interruption handling and call success rate
children.watch: Do not rank communications gross volume, annualized consumption and subscription ARR together.

children.name: Agent payments and commerce
children.thesis: Agent authorization, execution, settlement and dispute handling have to connect. Standards are driven by incumbents; the independent opportunity is in deliverable transaction and compliance steps.
children.bottleneck: Authorization, settlement, risk control and accountable transactions
children.watch: Protocol launches and strategic partnerships are not yet paid transaction volume.

domains.title: A · Physical base
domains.result: Usable compute that can be delivered and run reliably
domains.discipline: Look at process, reliability, delivery constraints and the capital cycle. Capacity expansion is not automatically a moat.
domains.boundary: Adjacent base layer: the agent-software event ledger does not cover the whole hardware industry.

domains.title: B · Compute and model serving
domains.resource: GPU and memory scheduling, training synchronization, inference throughput and latency
domains.buyer: Model training teams, application developers and agents
domains.result: Turning compute into usable model capability and low-cost inference and rollouts
domains.discipline: Distinguish capacity rental, performance engineering and training-inference-environment platforms. Check utilization, gross margin and committed capital.
domains.boundary: Training and inference coexist. The CPU control plane remains; the incremental bottleneck moves to GPUs, HBM and state.

domains.title: C · Data and feedback
domains.resource: Context, persistent state, expert tasks, environments and verifiers
domains.buyer: Enterprise data teams, agent applications and frontier labs
domains.result: Giving a task the right context and producing verifiable, reusable feedback
domains.discipline: Judge data software on architecture, state and performance. Judge data services on repeat purchase, delivery quality, gross margin and neutrality. Do not apply SaaS multiples to both.
domains.boundary: Evaluate storage and retrieval separately from data supply-chain services.

domains.title: D · Agent execution
domains.resource: Tools, sessions, sandboxes, state recovery and execution permissions
domains.buyer: Developers, enterprise business teams and machine callers
domains.result: Letting agents complete tasks in real systems continuously, reliably and auditably
domains.discipline: The unit of metering expands from requests to tasks, trajectories and outcomes. Check for paid execution rights and a data loop, not just framework usage.
domains.boundary: Security, identity, evaluation and the capital cycle cut across all four domains.

generations.title: RAG / Chain
generations.capability: Generation, embeddings and early tool calling. The reliable loop is mostly one round of retrieval followed by generation.
generations.architecture: retrieval → LLM; linear chains, early ReAct
generations.applications: Document Q&A, knowledge copilots, customer-support assistance
generations.scarcity: Access to private knowledge and retrieval quality
generations.profitPool: Parsing, retrieval, vector storage, RAG developer tools
generations.migration: Retrieval demand remains. Standalone vector features are being built into primary databases and platforms; differentiation moves to performance, hybrid retrieval and multimodal data.
outcomes: LangChain expanded across generations into development, deployment and evaluation
Qdrant has disclosed a new funding round
Chroma's Replit deal is kept at signed status

generations.title: Tool-use / Workflow
generations.capability: Tool selection and argument generation became more stable, so multi-step actions can be chained into flows.
generations.applications: Customer-support and sales automation, browser, voice and early coding agents
generations.scarcity: Connection to real systems, action permissions and execution success rate
generations.profitPool: Connectors, identity and authorization, search, browsers, sandboxes, tracing
generations.migration: Connection turns from technical integration into authorization and production consumption. Builders begin to diverge on distribution, durable execution and enterprise control.
outcomes: Flowise and Pipedream went to Workday
Open-source adoption and sign-ups still cannot stand in for evidence of paid use

generations.title: Reasoning / Protocol
generations.capability: Longer inference-time reasoning, continuous tool calling and open protocols.
generations.architecture: stateful loop, MCP / A2A, sandbox, memory, eval
generations.applications: Coding, deep research, cross-system business tasks
generations.scarcity: Controllable execution, model access, behavior observation and quality verifiers
generations.profitPool: Gateways, evals, observability, security and identity
generations.migration: Protocols lower connection friction. More of the value lands around the protocol: permissions, traffic, billing, policy and production data.
outcomes: A run of consolidation in observability and gateways
OpenRouter: signing and closing are tracked separately
W&B is an MLOps asset absorbed across generations, not a company born in this one

generations.title: Production Agent
generations.capability: Long tasks, sub-agents, context compaction, checkpoints and failure recovery.
generations.architecture: session / checkpoint / approval / files / tests / durable execution
generations.applications: Development, research, operations and SRE agents that can write to real systems
generations.scarcity: Long-lived state, isolated execution and recoverability
generations.profitPool: Agent clouds, durable runtimes, real-time transactional state and control planes
generations.migration: From selling a few lines of orchestration code to selling execution systems that keep running. The data layer expands from retrieval to local and shared state.
outcomes: Modal spans inference, sandboxes and post-training
Temporal is the commercial anchor for durable execution
Neon, Tecton and Fennel went into unified data platforms

generations.title: Learning / Verifiable Agent
generations.window: Emerging in 2025 H2, taking shape in 2026; in progress
generations.capability: Agentic RL, environment-based training, updatable memory and skills. Training and execution form a feedback loop.
generations.architecture: environment → rollout → verifier → RL / memory update
generations.applications: Automated R&D, finance and knowledge work, professional training tasks
generations.scarcity: Real task distributions, verifiable feedback and updatable state
generations.profitPool: RL environments, vertical verifiers, state and memory, machine search, identity and settlement
generations.migration: Data is not only corpus; it is also executable environments and professional verifiers. Keep the technical delivery of continual learning apart from valuation expectations.
outcomes: Environment suppliers already show funding and revenue signals
Deeptune's consolidation shows service platforms are also adding feedback capability
General verifiers, memory and payments still have to prove standalone revenue and repeat purchase

opportunities.product: Durable execution, isolated environments, failure recovery, task audit
opportunities.payer: Production agent applications / enterprise developer platforms
opportunities.logic: The more capable the model and the longer the task, the more real execution and recovery it consumes.
opportunities.test: Cost per successfully completed task, retention and expansion, failure recovery, gross margin
opportunities.risk: Bundling by clouds and model labs; falling redundant usage as agents get more efficient.

opportunities.product: Vertical RL environments, task distributions, simulation and reproducible evaluation
opportunities.payer: Lab post-training teams / enterprise model teams
opportunities.logic: Turning workflows into interactive tasks and delivering feedback that changes model capability, not just samples.
opportunities.test: Repeat purchase across models, environment difficulty updates, verifier reliability, data rights
opportunities.risk: Customer concentration, in-house builds and fast-aging environments. Funding heat is not sustained revenue.

opportunities.product: Multimodal data, real-time context, private and shared agent state
opportunities.payer: Enterprise data platforms / agent development teams
opportunities.logic: Tasks need to read and write state continuously. Value expands from one retrieval to managing data and execution together.
opportunities.test: Performance on real workloads, freshness, read-write isolation, migration cost and paid reuse
opportunities.risk: Native absorption by primary databases and lakehouses. A vector feature alone is not enough to price independently.

opportunities.product: Vertical verifiers, quality checking, uncontaminated evaluation and verifier services
opportunities.payer: Labs / buyers of high-stakes professional agents
opportunities.logic: General scoring is easily bundled. Domain verifiers need real outcomes, professional knowledge and continuous maintenance.
opportunities.test: Agreement between verifier and real outcomes, resistance to reward hacking, customer repeat purchase
opportunities.risk: Eval platforms, environment vendors and labs can all supply this. A gap in the statistics is not a gap in competition.

opportunities.product: Agent identity, delegated authorization, per-action policy and audit
opportunities.payer: Enterprise IT / security / owners of business systems
opportunities.logic: When machines perform write operations on behalf of people, permission and responsibility must attach to each action. The control plane can be reused across models.
opportunities.test: Delegation chains, least privilege, audit coverage, production customers and renewals
opportunities.risk: Distribution advantages of Okta, clouds and security platforms. General auth is not an unoccupied new market.

opportunities.product: Expert tasks, data integration, quality checking and environment delivery services
opportunities.payer: Lab procurement / professional enterprise model teams
opportunities.logic: Software sells reusable capability; services sell supply, quality and delivery. The two economic structures must be analyzed separately.
opportunities.test: Net revenue vs pass-through volume, gross margin, repeat purchase, expert supply and neutrality
opportunities.risk: Large-customer concentration, labor-intensive delivery, data contamination, rights and conflicts of interest.

opportunities.product: Inference engines, KV and state management, heterogeneous memory scheduling
opportunities.payer: Model-serving platforms / buyers of inference at scale
opportunities.logic: GPU, memory and communication constraints create value for software optimization, but customers must be shown to keep paying for it.
opportunities.test: Throughput and cost for tasks of equal quality, portability across hardware, economic value retained
opportunities.risk: Productization by NVIDIA, model labs and open-source engines. A single optimization may be erased by the next release.

opportunities.product: Transaction authorization, merchant onboarding, execution, settlement and dispute handling
opportunities.payer: Agent service providers / merchants / payment institutions
opportunities.logic: Protocols lower integration friction. Startup value has to be proven by real paid transactions and a mechanism for bearing risk.
opportunities.test: Settled transactions, net take rate, failure and fraud losses, and reuse
opportunities.risk: Incumbents lead the standards. Protocol adoption, partnership announcements and funding are not transaction revenue.

research.principle: Read the generations by the loop models can reliably complete. Read the opportunities by the resources outside that loop that remain scarce, measurable and independently deliverable.
